title: Module 1 - Governance, Risk, and Compliance - Part 15

questions.learningObjective: Summarize the information security challenges associated with artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.
questions.topic: AI supply chain and model governance
questions.stem: A vendor model is updated silently and changes its detection recommendations. Which elements belong in the design package? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: An AI model is a critical dependency needing lifecycle governance. To control silent vendor updates, the package must record model versions (A), define rollback triggers (B), and test behavior changes (C). Classifying inputs (D) and auditing prompt/output handling (E) are data-leakage controls, not supply-chain governance.

whyWrong.D: Classifying allowed inputs controls data leakage, not version change.
whyWrong.E: Auditing prompt and output handling addresses leakage, not supply-chain governance.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.5: Summarize the information security challenges associated with artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.

whyCorrect.A: Recording model versions makes silent updates visible and traceable.
whyCorrect.B: Rollback triggers let you revert to a known-good model when behavior degrades.
whyCorrect.C: Testing behavior changes detects when an update shifts detection results before harm occurs.

questions.learningObjective: Given a set of organizational security requirements, implement the appropriate governance components.
questions.stem: An emergency firewall change skipped review and later broke a regulated data feed. Which elements belong in the design package? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Change and configuration governance keeps emergency speed while staying accountable. The pieces that close this gap are classifying emergency changes (D), requiring rollback plans (C), and performing a post-change review (A). Minimizing data (B) is staging-data governance, and recording exceptions/recertification dates (E) is a procedure concern—both off-topic here.

whyWrong.B: Minimizing data before use is staging-data governance, not change control.
whyWrong.E: Recording exceptions and recertification dates is a procedure/policy concern, not emergency-change control.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.1: Given a set of organizational security requirements, implement the appropriate governance components.

whyCorrect.A: A post-change review captures impact and lessons, turning the bypass into accountable evidence.
whyCorrect.C: A rollback plan lets a failed emergency change be reversed before it breaks production.
whyCorrect.D: Classifying emergency changes sets the risk-based approval path so review is not simply skipped.

questions.learningObjective: Summarize the information security challenges associated with artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.
questions.stem: Phishing volume rises and messages are highly tailored to internal projects. Which evidence points would let a reviewer defend the decision against plausible alternatives? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: AI-amplified phishing calls for updates to detection, awareness, and response. The defensible evidence is hardening reporting workflows (A), monitoring impersonation patterns (D), and training against targeted lures (E). Auditing prompt/output handling (B) is a data-leakage control and defining rollback triggers (C) is supply-chain governance—both off-topic.

whyWrong.B: Auditing prompt and output handling addresses AI data leakage, not phishing.
whyWrong.C: Defining rollback triggers governs the AI supply chain, not adversary activity.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.5: Summarize the information security challenges associated with artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.

whyCorrect.A: Hardened reporting workflows speed user-driven detection of tailored phishing.
whyCorrect.D: Monitoring impersonation patterns catches AI-crafted lures mimicking internal projects.
whyCorrect.E: Training against targeted lures raises resistance to the personalized attacks described.

questions.learningObjective: Given a set of organizational security requirements, perform risk management activities.
questions.stem: A vendor will administer a security platform and can view incident evidence. Which root cause is most important to address?

choices.A: Review contractual duties, access scope, logging, subprocessors, breach notification, and offboarding controls
choices.B: Combine quantitative estimates with qualitative business, safety, legal, and reputation factors
choices.C: Assess data, model, output, automation, privacy, and accountability risks before operational use
choices.D: Apply compensating controls, document residual risk, and obtain accountable risk acceptance
choices.E: Run a business impact analysis and turn impact tolerance into recovery and continuity requirements

questions.explanation: A vendor administering your platform becomes part of your own security and audit surface. Third-party risk management is the right lens: define contractual duties, access scope, logging, subprocessors, breach notification, and offboarding—choice A. The other options handle internal risk analysis, AI risk, treatment, or recovery, not the vendor relationship itself.

whyWrong.B: Quantitative/qualitative analysis compares risks; it does not set vendor obligations.
whyWrong.C: AI usage risk assessment is the wrong domain for vendor administration.
whyWrong.D: Compensating controls and acceptance treat residual risk, not the vendor contract.
whyWrong.E: A business impact analysis sizes recovery needs, not third-party controls.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.2: Given a set of organizational security requirements, perform risk management activities.

whyCorrect.A: It governs the vendor as part of your audit surface—access, logging, breach, and termination obligations.

questions.learningObjective: Summarize the information security challenges associated with artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.
questions.stem: An AI assistant retrieves external web content and can open tickets or trigger workflows. Which controls or evidence should be included? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: When untrusted content can drive actions, prompt injection and tool misuse are the core risks. The controls that close them are requiring approval for actions (A), scoping tool identity (B), and separating untrusted instructions (D). Redacting fields (C) is a data-leakage control that can limit injection-driven exfiltration, and requiring corroborating signals (E) is an output-reliability control that helps with untrusted output—useful, but neither is the strongest control for the tool-misuse path this scenario keys.

whyWrong.C: Redacting sensitive fields is a data-leakage control that can reduce injection-driven exfiltration, but it does not constrain the injected actions themselves.
whyWrong.E: Requiring corroborating signals supports output reliability and untrusted-output handling, but it is not the strongest control for tool misuse here.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.5: Summarize the information security challenges associated with artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.

whyCorrect.A: Requiring approval for actions adds a human gate before high-impact operations.
whyCorrect.B: Scoping tool identity limits what the assistant can do if manipulated.
whyCorrect.D: Separating untrusted instructions stops injected text from being treated as commands.

questions.learningObjective: Explain how compliance affects information security strategies.
questions.stem: A product roadmap plans to collect device identifiers, support notes, and behavior telemetry for a new personalization feature. Which elements belong in the design package? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Privacy is a lifecycle design rule applied before collection. The package should validate purpose (A), define retention and access (B), and minimize collection (C). Verifying period of coverage (D) is an audit concern and retaining audit evidence (E) is a sector-compliance task—both adjacent but not the lifecycle controls here.

whyWrong.D: Verifying period of coverage relates to audit scoping, not privacy lifecycle design.
whyWrong.E: Retaining audit evidence supports sector compliance, not lifecycle limitation.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.3: Explain how compliance affects information security strategies.

whyCorrect.A: Validating purpose ensures the collection is justified rather than speculative.
whyCorrect.B: Defining retention and access limits how long and to whom the data is exposed.
whyCorrect.C: Minimizing collection reduces the data footprint and downstream privacy risk.

questions.learningObjective: Given a scenario, perform threat modeling activities.
questions.stem: A retrieval-augmented assistant can read internal documents and create support tickets. Which elements belong in the design package? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: An AI workflow that reads internal data and takes actions adds model, data, and action surfaces, so AI-specific threat modeling applies. The package should log retrieved context (A), separate read and act privileges (B), and gate external instructions (E). Mapping threats to assets (C) and validating exposure paths (D) are threat-profiling steps, not the AI-model controls.

whyWrong.C: Mapping threats to assets is threat profiling, not AI-model control design.
whyWrong.D: Validating exposure paths is a threat-profiling step, not an AI-model control.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.4: Given a scenario, perform threat modeling activities.

whyCorrect.A: Logging retrieved context makes the data feeding the model auditable.
whyCorrect.B: Separating read and act privileges prevents a read path from triggering unsafe actions.
whyCorrect.E: Gating external instructions blocks injected content from driving the assistant's actions.

questions.learningObjective: Given a set of organizational security requirements, perform risk management activities.
questions.stem: Leadership wants to compare ransomware-outage risk against payment-fraud risk using both expected loss and strategic impact. Which approach best addresses the issue?

choices.A: Run a business impact analysis and turn impact tolerance into recovery and continuity requirements
choices.B: Apply compensating controls, document residual risk, and obtain accountable risk acceptance
choices.C: Assess data, model, output, automation, privacy, and accountability risks before operational use
choices.D: Review contractual duties, access scope, logging, subprocessors, breach notification, and offboarding controls
choices.E: Combine quantitative estimates with qualitative business, safety, legal, and reputation factors

questions.explanation: Comparing these risks on both expected loss and strategic impact needs both numeric and contextual evidence. The answer is E: pair expected-loss estimates with business, safety, legal, and reputation factors and state the assumptions. The other options treat risk, assess AI risk, set recovery targets, or review vendors—none blends both lenses for this comparison.

whyWrong.A: A business impact analysis sizes recovery needs, not a quantitative-plus-qualitative comparison.
whyWrong.B: Compensating controls and acceptance treat a risk; they do not analyze and compare two.
whyWrong.C: AI usage risk assessment is the wrong domain for ransomware-versus-fraud comparison.
whyWrong.D: Third-party risk review covers vendors, not this internal risk comparison.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.2: Given a set of organizational security requirements, perform risk management activities.

whyCorrect.E: It blends quantitative loss estimates with qualitative impact factors, the only fair way to compare these two risks.

questions.learningObjective: Given a set of organizational security requirements, implement the appropriate governance components.
questions.stem: Developers copied production customer records into a shared test environment to troubleshoot faster. Which evidence points would let a reviewer defend the decision against plausible alternatives? (Select all that apply.)

choices.D: Document workflow steps and required evidence
choices.E: Define consulted legal and security roles

questions.explanation: Nonproduction environments still carry data-protection duties. The defensible controls are masking or tokenizing sensitive fields (A), minimizing data before use (B), and expiring test copies (C). Documenting workflow steps (D) is a procedure concern and naming consulted roles (E) is a RACI concern—neither protects the staging data.

whyWrong.D: Documenting workflow steps is a procedure artifact, not a staging-data control.
whyWrong.E: Defining consulted roles is decision ownership, not data protection.

sources: CAS005 LO 1.1: Given a set of organizational security requirements, implement the appropriate governance components.

whyCorrect.A: Tokenizing replaces sensitive values with tokens (mapping kept in a vault) and masking obscures them, so test data does not expose real customer values.
whyCorrect.B: Minimizing data before use limits how much sensitive data ever reaches the test environment.
whyCorrect.C: Expiring test copies stops production data from lingering in staging indefinitely.

The answer is E: estimate exposure and frequency quantitatively, then weigh business, safety, legal, and reputation factors and state the assumptions. The other options assess AI risk, set recovery targets, treat risk, or review vendors—none combines both lenses.
